mcqs.q: An articulator is defined as a mechanical instrument that represents:
opts: The maxilla and its relationship to the cranial base
The mandible and the muscles of mastication
The occlusal plane and the curve of Spee
mcqs.explain: An articulator is a mechanical instrument that represents the temporomandibular joints AND jaws.

mcqs.q: The full definition of an articulator states that casts may be attached to it in order to:
opts: Simulate some or all mandibular movements
Simulate all mandibular movements without exception
Measure the vertical dimension of occlusion
mcqs.explain: The phrase is 'to simulate SOME OR ALL mandibular movements' — the 'some or all' is what allows for the four different classes.

mcqs.q: The two mandibular movements an articulator is principally asked to reproduce are:
mcqs.explain: The lecture names the lateral and protrusive movements as those the instrument reproduces.

mcqs.q: The articulator helps to maintain the desired maxillomandibular relationship of the casts during tooth arrangement. The direct consequence of this is that:
opts: Teeth can be arranged in the absence of the patient
The vertical dimension need not be recorded clinically
The centric relation record can be taken in the laboratory
mcqs.explain: Because the relationship is held, it becomes possible to arrange teeth in the absence of the patient.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT one of the five listed uses of an articulator?
opts: Mounting dental casts for diagnosis, treatment planning and patient presentation
Wax-up and refining the occlusion for dental restorations
mcqs.explain: The five uses are mounting casts for diagnosis/planning/presentation, arranging artificial teeth, wax-up and refining the occlusion, studying occlusion and mandibular movements, and aiding fabrication of restorations and lost dental parts.

mcqs.q: The first listed use of an articulator covers three purposes. Which set is correct?
opts: Diagnosis, treatment planning and patient presentation
Diagnosis, impression making and patient presentation
Treatment planning, tooth selection and shade matching
Diagnosis, treatment planning and post-insertion review
mcqs.explain: Mounting dental casts serves diagnosis, treatment planning and patient presentation.

mcqs.q: Arrangement of artificial teeth on an articulator applies to:
mcqs.explain: The stated use is arrangement of artificial teeth for complete AND removable partial dentures.

mcqs.q: The fifth listed use of an articulator is to aid in the fabrication of:
opts: Dental restorations and lost dental parts
mcqs.explain: It aids in the fabrication of dental restorations and lost dental parts.

mcqs.q: The four classes of articulator are, in order:
mcqs.explain: Class I non-adjustable, Class II average-value, Class III semi-adjustable, Class IV fully-adjustable.

mcqs.q: Which class of articulator is also known as a simple hinge or plane line articulator?
mcqs.explain: Class I non-adjustable articulators are also called simple hinge or plane line articulators.

mcqs.q: A Class I articulator is described as a simple holding instrument capable of accepting:
opts: A face-bow transfer and a centric record
mcqs.explain: It is a simple holding instrument capable of accepting a single static registration.

mcqs.q: On a Class I articulator, which motion is possible?
mcqs.explain: On a Class I articulator, vertical motion is possible — there is no horizontal movement.

mcqs.q: Which class is also known as the mean value articulator?
mcqs.explain: Class II average-value articulators are also called mean value articulators.

mcqs.q: A Class II articulator is defined as an instrument that permits horizontal as well as vertical motion, BUT:
opts: Does not orient the motion to the temporomandibular joints via a face-bow transfer
Does not permit any protrusive movement of the lower member
Cannot accept a centric relation record taken from the patient
Cannot hold more than one pair of mounted casts at a time
mcqs.explain: The defining limitation is that it does not orient the motion to the TMJs via a face-bow transfer.

mcqs.q: The horizontal condylar guidance of an average-value articulator is:
opts: Adjustable from the patient's protrusive record
mcqs.explain: The Class II instrument has a fixed horizontal condylar guidance of 30 degrees.

mcqs.q: Which of the following about a Class II articulator is NOT true?
opts: It has an adjustable incisal guide table
It allows a limited range of protrusive and lateral movements
It has a fixed inter-condylar distance
It has a fixed horizontal condylar guidance
mcqs.explain: The Class II articulator has a FIXED incisal guidance; the adjustable incisal guide table belongs to the semi-adjustable instrument.

mcqs.q: The range of protrusive and lateral movement permitted by a Class II articulator is described as:
opts: Equal to that of a fully-adjustable instrument
mcqs.explain: It allows a limited range of protrusive and lateral movements.

mcqs.q: The word 'average' in 'average-value articulator' refers to the fact that:
opts: Its guidance values are population averages rather than measurements from the patient
It is of average cost compared with other instruments
It reproduces the average of the right and left condylar paths
Its accuracy lies midway between a Class I and a Class IV instrument in every respect
mcqs.explain: The fixed condylar guidance, incisal guidance and intercondylar distance are all averages taken from populations, not values measured from the individual patient.

mcqs.q: The Bonwill triangle is described as an equilateral triangle of which side length?
mcqs.explain: It is a 4-inch equilateral triangle.

mcqs.q: The Bonwill triangle is bounded by lines connecting:
opts: The mandibular incisal edge to each condyle, and condyle to condyle
The two condyles and the midpoint of the hard palate
The hinge axis and the two hamular notches
The incisive papilla and the two canine tips
mcqs.explain: The lines connect the contact points of the mandibular central incisor's incisal edge (or the mid-line of the mandibular residual ridge) to each condyle, and from one condyle to the other.

mcqs.q: In an edentulous patient, what substitutes for the mandibular central incisor contact point in the Bonwill triangle?
opts: The mid-line of the mandibular residual ridge
The mid-line of the maxillary residual ridge
mcqs.explain: The definition allows the mid-line of the mandibular residual ridge in place of the incisal contact point.

mcqs.q: In the Bonwill triangle, which point of the condyle is usually taken?
mcqs.explain: The lines run to each condyle, usually its mid point.

mcqs.q: The Bonwill triangle is named after a dentist of which nationality and dates?
mcqs.explain: William Gibson Arlington Bonwill, American dentist, 1833–1899.

mcqs.q: In what year is the Bonwill triangle dated in this lecture?
mcqs.explain: The triangle is labelled BONWILL 1858.

mcqs.q: Bonwill's own articulator is described as a:
mcqs.explain: It is Bonwill's brass wire anatomical articulator.

mcqs.q: The side length of the mean value articulator's triangle is given in millimetres as:
mcqs.explain: The mean value articulator carries 100 mm sides — the metric equivalent of Bonwill's 4 inches.

mcqs.q: Which feature is shared by BOTH Class I and Class II articulators?
opts: Vertical motion is possible on each
Both permit a limited lateral excursion
mcqs.explain: Vertical motion is possible on both; horizontal motion, the 30-degree guidance and the lateral excursion belong to Class II alone.

mcqs.q: A clinician mounts casts on an instrument that opens and closes but will not move the lower cast forward at all. The instrument is:
mcqs.explain: No horizontal motion at all means a simple hinge — a Class I, non-adjustable articulator.

mcqs.q: An instrument permits a short protrusive excursion down a track fixed at 30°, has a fixed incisal guidance and a fixed intercondylar distance, and takes no face-bow. It is:
mcqs.explain: Fixed 30° guidance, fixed incisal guidance, fixed intercondylar distance and no face-bow orientation together define the Class II average-value instrument.

mcqs.q: Why is the Bonwill triangle discussed in a lecture about articulators rather than only in one about anatomy?
opts: Because the average-value articulator is built directly on its geometry
Because it determines the steepness of the condylar guidance
Because it is the only way to locate the hinge axis
Because it defines the position of the incisal guide pin on every instrument
mcqs.explain: Bonwill's brass wire anatomical articulator, and the mean value articulators descended from it, are built on the triangle's geometry — the instrument is the triangle rendered in metal.

mcqs.q: Which statement best describes the relationship between the four classes of articulator?
opts: They form a ladder of capability, from one static record and a hinge up to three-plane adjustability
They are four competing designs of equal capability
They differ only in the material from which they are made
They are distinguished solely by whether they are arcon or non-arcon
mcqs.explain: The classes represent increasing capability, from a holding instrument accepting a single static record to one adjustable in three planes.

mcqs.q: On which member of a Class II articulator is the incisal guide pin found to rest?
opts: On a fixed incisal guide table
On an adjustable incisal guide table
It has no incisal guide pin
mcqs.explain: A Class II articulator has fixed incisal guidance, so the pin rests on a fixed guide table.

saqs.a: A MECHANICAL INSTRUMENT THAT REPRESENTS THE TEMPOROMANDIBULAR JOINTS AND JAWS, to which MAXILLARY AND MANDIBULAR CASTS may be attached to SIMULATE SOME OR ALL MANDIBULAR MOVEMENTS.

ans.text: A mechanical instrument that represents the temporomandibular joints and jaws, to which maxillary and mandibular casts may be attached to simulate some or all mandibular movements.

saqs.q: Explain how an articulator makes laboratory work possible.
saqs.a: It helps to MAINTAIN THE DESIRED MAXILLOMANDIBULAR RELATIONSHIP OF THE CASTS DURING TOOTH ARRANGEMENT. Thus it MAKES IT POSSIBLE TO ARRANGE TEETH IN THE ABSENCE OF THE PATIENT.

ans.text: It maintains the desired maxillomandibular relationship of the casts during tooth arrangement — which is what makes it possible to arrange teeth in the absence of the patient.

saqs.q: List the five uses of an articulator.
saqs.a: (1) MOUNTING DENTAL CASTS for diagnosis, treatment planning and patient presentation. (2) ARRANGEMENT OF ARTIFICIAL TEETH for complete and removable partial dentures. (3) WAX-UP AND REFINING THE OCCLUSION for dental restorations. (4) STUDYING OCCLUSION AND MANDIBULAR MOVEMENTS. (5) AIDING IN FABRICATION OF DENTAL RESTORATIONS AND LOST DENTAL PARTS.

list: Mounting dental casts — for diagnosis, treatment planning and patient presentation
Arrangement of artificial teeth — for complete and removable partial dentures
Wax-up and refining the occlusion for dental restorations
Aiding in fabrication of dental restorations and lost dental parts

saqs.q: Give the classification of articulators by class and name.
saqs.a: CLASS I — NON-ADJUSTABLE articulators. CLASS II — AVERAGE-VALUE articulators. CLASS III — SEMI-ADJUSTABLE articulators. CLASS IV — FULLY-ADJUSTABLE articulators.

saqs.q: Describe the Class I articulator, including its alternative names.
saqs.a: Also called the SIMPLE HINGE or PLANE LINE articulator. It is a SIMPLE HOLDING INSTRUMENT capable of accepting A SINGLE STATIC REGISTRATION. VERTICAL MOTION IS POSSIBLE — it opens and closes and nothing more, so neither protrusion nor lateral excursion can be reproduced on it.

ans.text: Also called the simple hinge or plane line articulator.

list: A simple holding instrument, capable of accepting a single static registration
Vertical motion only — it opens and closes and nothing more
So neither protrusion nor lateral excursion can be reproduced on it

saqs.a: Also called the MEAN VALUE articulator. It is an instrument that PERMITS HORIZONTAL AS WELL AS VERTICAL MOTION, BUT DOES NOT ORIENT THE MOTION TO THE TEMPOROMANDIBULAR JOINTS VIA A FACE-BOW TRANSFER.

ans.text: Also called the mean value articulator — an instrument that permits horizontal as well as vertical motion, but does not orient the motion to the temporomandibular joints via a face-bow transfer.

saqs.q: List the four features of a Class II average-value articulator.
saqs.a: (1) It allows a LIMITED RANGE of protrusive and lateral movements. (2) It has a FIXED HORIZONTAL CONDYLAR GUIDANCE OF 30 DEGREES. (3) It has a FIXED INCISAL GUIDANCE. (4) It has a FIXED INTER-CONDYLAR DISTANCE.

list: Allows a limited range of protrusive and lateral movements

saqs.q: Why is the Class II instrument called an 'average-value' articulator?
saqs.a: Because every one of its guidance values — the 30° condylar guidance, the incisal guidance and the intercondylar distance — is an AVERAGE taken from populations rather than a measurement from the individual patient. That is both what the name means and where its limitation lies.

ans.text: Because every one of its guidance values — the 30° condylar guidance, the incisal guidance and the intercondylar distance — is an average taken from populations, rather than a measurement from the individual patient. That is both what the name means and where its limitation lies.

saqs.q: Define the Bonwill triangle, and name the man and the year.
saqs.a: An eponym for a 4-INCH EQUILATERAL TRIANGLE bounded by lines connecting THE CONTACT POINTS OF THE MANDIBULAR CENTRAL INCISOR'S INCISAL EDGE (or the mid-line of the mandibular residual ridge) TO EACH CONDYLE (usually its mid point), and FROM ONE CONDYLE TO THE OTHER. Named after William Gibson Arlington Bonwill, American dentist, 1833–1899, and dated 1858.

ans.text: An eponym for a 4-inch equilateral triangle, bounded by lines connecting the contact points of the mandibular central incisor's incisal edge — or the mid-line of the mandibular residual ridge — to each condyle (usually its mid point), and from one condyle to the other.
Named after William Gibson Arlington Bonwill, American dentist, 1833–1899; dated 1858.

saqs.q: What connects the Bonwill triangle to the mean value articulator?
saqs.a: BONWILL'S BRASS WIRE ANATOMICAL ARTICULATOR was built directly on the geometry of the triangle, and the mean value articulators descended from it carry the same geometry — sides of 100 mm, the metric equivalent of Bonwill's 4 inches, condyle to condyle and each condyle to the incisal point. The average-value instrument is the Bonwill triangle rendered in metal, which is why its intercondylar distance is fixed.

ans.text: Bonwill's brass wire anatomical articulator was built directly on the geometry of the triangle, and the mean value articulators descended from it carry the same geometry — sides of 100 mm, the metric equivalent of Bonwill's 4 inches, condyle to condyle and each condyle to the incisal point. The average-value instrument is the Bonwill triangle rendered in metal — which is why its intercondylar distance is fixed.

saqs.q: Compare the Class I and Class II articulators under the headings: motion permitted, condylar guidance, incisal guidance and intercondylar distance.
saqs.a: MOTION — Class I: vertical only; Class II: vertical AND a limited range of horizontal. CONDYLAR GUIDANCE — Class I: none; Class II: FIXED at 30°. INCISAL GUIDANCE — Class I: none; Class II: FIXED. INTERCONDYLAR DISTANCE — Class I: not applicable; Class II: FIXED at the 100 mm Bonwill side. Neither orients the casts to the joints by a face-bow; the Class I accepts only a single static registration.

head: CLASS I
CLASS II
rows: vertical and a limited range of horizontal — protrusive and lateral

ans.text: Neither instrument orients the casts to the joints by a face-bow, and the Class I accepts only a single static registration.

saqs.q: Which movement capability separates a Class I from a Class II articulator, and what capability do both still lack?
saqs.a: HORIZONTAL MOTION separates them — Class I permits vertical motion only, while Class II permits horizontal as well as vertical motion, though in a LIMITED range. Both still lack ORIENTATION OF THE MOTION TO THE TEMPOROMANDIBULAR JOINTS BY A FACE-BOW TRANSFER, and so neither can be set from the individual patient's own condylar path.
